papers.full_text: Article summary Vaccine hesitancy poses a significant challenge to achieving optimal immunization coverage, particularly in regions like Nigeria where measles remains a public health threat. This study identified key determinants of measles vaccine hesitancy among caregivers in Ogun State, revealing that younger caregiver age, cultural or religious beliefs, and logistical barriers such as vaccine availability and travel time to facilities significantly influence hesitancy levels. Abstract Background Measles remains a major public health concern in Nigeria despite the availability of effective vaccines. Vaccine hesitancy among caregivers threatens the achievement of optimal immunization coverage this study assessed the determinants of measles vaccine hesitancy among caregivers of under-five children in Ado-Odo/Ota and Odeda Local Government Areas of Ogun State. Methods A mixed-methods cross-sectional study was conducted among 368 caregivers selected using a multistage sampling technique. Quantitative data were collected using structured questionnaires and analyzed using IBM SPSS version 27. Descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and logistic regression were used to determine associations and predictors of vaccine hesitancy. Qualitative data were collected through six focus group discussions with 42 caregivers and analyzed using QualCoder V.3.8.2. Results The prevalence of vaccine hesitancy was 44.6%. At the individual level, age group was significantly associated with vaccine hesitancy (p = 0.028), with younger caregivers more likely to be hesitant. Knowledge (p = 0.774) and attitude (p = 0.442) were not significantly associated with vaccine hesitancy in multivariate analysis. However, qualitative findings revealed substantial gaps in schedule-specific knowledge. At the health system level, vaccine availability (p = 0.031) and time to facility (p = 0.004) were significantly associated with hesitancy. At the community level, cultural and religious influences were significant (p = 0.011). Logistic regression identified younger caregiver age (AOR = 1.91; 95% CI: 1.10–3.32; reference: age 38–49 years), cultural or religious beliefs that discourage vaccination (AOR = 0.52; 95% CI: 0.31–0.86; reference: beliefs that discourage vaccination), travel time of less than 30 min to the vaccination facility (AOR = 0.44; 95% CI: 0.22–0.90; reference: travel time exceeding one hour), and consistent vaccine availability (AOR = 0.63; 95% CI: 0.39–0.99; reference: experience of vaccine stock-outs) as significant predictors. Conclusion Measles vaccine hesitancy is significantly associated with structural, community, and interpersonal factors. Similar content being viewed by others 1 Introduction Vaccine hesitancy has emerged as a major global public health challenge, undermining immunization programmes and contributing to the persistence of vaccine-preventable diseases despite the availability of effective vaccines. It is defined as the delay in acceptance or refusal of vaccination despite the availability of vaccination services and is influenced by complex behavioural and social factors that vary across settings [1, 2]. Recent evidence suggests that vaccine hesitancy remains substantial globally, with prevalence estimates ranging between 25% and 42% across different populations, driven largely by misinformation, declining trust in institutions, and evolving perceptions of vaccine risk [3]. Measles, one of the most contagious vaccine-preventable diseases, continues to pose a significant global health threat, particularly among children under five years of age. Despite the availability of safe and effective vaccines, measles has re-emerged in many regions due to suboptimal immunization coverage. In 2023, over 10 million measles cases were reported globally, reflecting persistent gaps in vaccination coverage below the 95% threshold required for herd immunity [4]. In low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), including Nigeria, these gaps are further exacerbated by systemic health challenges and demand-side barriers that limit vaccine uptake [5]. Vaccination decisions are shaped by cultural and religious influences, which vary across settings and can affect caregiver acceptance of childhood vaccines [6]. In addition, vaccine hesitancy has been demonstrated to be a measurable and relevant challenge for childhood immunization, with caregivers’ knowledge, attitudes, and socio-demographic characteristics significantly associated with hesitancy and vaccination behavior [7]. Globally, efforts to control measles and other vaccine-preventable diseases are increasingly undermined by insufficient immunization coverage. In Europe, vaccine hesitancy has emerged as a major barrier to achieving adequate vaccination rates, whereas in regions such as sub-Saharan Africa, coverage challenges often result from a combination of factors including limited access and vaccine availability [8]. In Ethiopia, studies have identified fear of side effects, misconceptions about vaccine safety, and low confidence in immunization services as significant predictors of vaccine hesitancy, with evidence suggesting that effective communication and community engagement can improve trust and correct misinformation [9]. In Nigeria, measles remains a major contributor to childhood morbidity and mortality, with recurrent outbreaks reported across multiple states. National immunization coverage remains suboptimal, and recent surveillance reports indicate thousands of confirmed measles cases annually, reflecting both structural weaknesses and behavioural barriers to vaccination [10, 11]. Ogun State, despite relatively stronger immunization infrastructure compared to other regions, continues to experience recurring measles cases, suggesting that factors beyond vaccine availability contribute to persistent immunity gaps. Nigeria’s linguistic and cultural diversity presents challenges for vaccination promotion, particularly among rural and less-educated populations where access to and comprehension of vaccine information may be limited. Evidence shows that the use of local languages in health education improves caregivers’ knowledge and attitudes toward vaccination [12]. Caregiver decision-making is further influenced by perceptions of vaccine risks and benefits, trust in healthcare providers, religious beliefs, and prevailing social norms, with lower trust and safety concerns commonly associated with vaccine hesitancy [13]. Evidence from LMICs indicates that vaccination uptake is shaped by a combination of demographic, socioeconomic, service-related, and belief-based factors [14]. Health system barriers such as long waiting times, vaccine stockouts, and negative interactions with healthcare workers have been consistently associated with incomplete immunization uptake [15]. In addition, misinformation, distrust in health systems, and community-level narratives have been identified as key drivers of vaccine hesitancy, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa [16]. Cultural and religious beliefs further shape caregivers’ vaccination decisions, with evidence showing that such influences may either promote or hinder vaccine acceptance depending on local context [17]. Vaccine decision-making is therefore influenced by multiple interacting factors operating at individual, interpersonal, community, and health system levels, as conceptualized by the Social Ecological Model [18]. This multilevel perspective is particularly relevant in settings where vaccines are available but uptake remains suboptimal, highlighting the need to understand how these determinants interact within specific local contexts. Caregiver vaccine hesitancy is influenced by a combination of individual and contextual factors, including limited knowledge, concerns about adverse effects, misinformation, religious beliefs, and constraints related to access and resources. Evidence from systematic reviews and cross-sectional studies consistently identifies lack of reliable vaccine information, fear of side effects, and cultural or faith-based beliefs as key drivers of delayed or refused vaccination across settings [19, 20]. Misinformation and limited access to credible health information further amplify safety concerns, while socioeconomic barriers such as transportation costs and competing priorities compound these effects. Religious and cultural influences remain particularly important, with evidence showing that faith-based beliefs may either promote or hinder vaccine uptake depending on context [21]. Community engagement strategies, including collaboration with trusted religious and traditional leaders, have been shown to effectively address misinformation and improve vaccine uptake [22]. Despite extensive research on vaccine hesitancy globally and nationally, there remains limited localized evidence examining how these multi-level determinants operate within specific communities in Ogun State. Ado-Odo/Ota and Odeda LGAs differ in terms of urbanization, access to health services, and sociocultural dynamics, yet empirical data on vaccine hesitancy within these areas remain scarce. This study therefore assessed the determinants of measles vaccine hesitancy among caregivers of under-five children in Ado-Odo/Ota and Odeda LGAs of Ogun State using a mixed-methods approach. 2 Conceptual framework The Social Ecological Model (SEM) guided the selection and interpretation of study variables. Individual-level factors included caregivers’ age, educational status, knowledge, and attitudes towards measles vaccination. Interpersonal factors comprised social, cultural, and religious influences on vaccination decisions. Community-level factors were explored through focus group discussions and included prevailing community beliefs and norms regarding childhood vaccination. Health-system factors included vaccine availability and accessibility of vaccination services, such as travel time to health facilities. The SEM was further used to organize and integrate the quantitative and qualitative findings. 3 Methods 3.1 Study design A mixed-methods cross-sectional study design was employed to assess the determinants of measles vaccine hesitancy among caregivers of under-five children. The quantitative component utilized a descriptive cross-sectional approach to examine associations between socio-demographic, healthcare service-related, and psychosocial factors and vaccine hesitancy. The qualitative component complemented these findings by exploring caregivers’ experiences, beliefs, and contextual influences through focus group discussions (FGDs), enabling triangulation of results. To reflect this design, the Methods section is organized into two subsections: the Quantitative Survey and the Qualitative Interviews. 3.2 Study setting The study was conducted in Ado-Odo/Ota and Odeda Local Government Areas (LGAs) of Ogun State, Nigeria. Ogun State is located in the South-West geopolitical zone of Nigeria and shares boundaries with Lagos, Oyo, and Ondo States. Ado-Odo/Ota is predominantly urban and industrial, whereas Odeda is semi-urban with significant rural settlements. These LGAs were purposively selected due to their contrasting socio-demographic characteristics and documented occurrence of measles cases between 2022 and 2024. While Ado-Odo/Ota is densely populated with diverse populations, Odeda has experienced recurrent outbreaks despite immunization efforts. Findings from this study are therefore context specific. 3.3 Quantitative survey 3.3.1 Study population The study population comprised caregivers (mothers, fathers, and guardians) of children aged 0–59 months residing in the selected LGAs. 3.3.2 Eligibility criteria Caregivers who had resided in the study areas for at least six months, had children aged 0–59 months, and provided informed consent were included. Caregivers who were not directly responsible for immunization decisions or declined participation were excluded. 3.3.3 Sample size determination The sample size was determined using the Cochran formula for single proportions: Where: n = minimum sample size, Z = standard normal deviate at 95% confidence level (1.96), p = estimated prevalence of vaccine hesitancy (0.32), d = margin of error (0.05). The minimum sample size was determined using Cochran formula and based on a vaccine hesitancy prevalence of 32% [23]. Substituting these values yielded a minimum sample size of 334. After adjusting for a 10% non-response rate, the final sample size was 368 participants. Due to the multistage sampling design, proportional allocation was applied across selected LGAs and wards to ensure representativeness of the study population. A design effect was not applied in the sample size calculation. This was because the intra-cluster correlation coefficient (ICC) for vaccine hesitancy was unknown in this setting, and published ICC estimates for immunization outcomes in similar Nigerian contexts were not available. Post-hoc sensitivity analysis indicated that the achieved sample size of 368 would still provide adequate power (≥ 80%) to detect an odds ratio of 1.5 or greater for key predictors, assuming a design effect of up to 2.0. This is acknowledged as a limitation of the study. 3.3.4 Sampling technique and procedure A multistage sampling technique was employed in selecting study participants. Stage 1 Ado-Odo/Ota LGA (16 wards) and Odeda LGA (10 wards) were included in the study. To ensure representativeness, 50% of wards were selected from each LGA using simple random sampling by balloting. Accordingly, eight wards were selected from Ado-Odo/Ota LGA and five wards from Odeda LGA. Following sample size determination, proportionate allocation was used to distribute the study sample across the two LGAs based on their estimated populations of under-five children (Table 1). The number of respondents allocated to each LGA and ward was determined by dividing the estimated under-five population of the LGA or ward by the total under-five population of the study area and multiplying by the total sample size. The allocated sample was subsequently distributed proportionately among the selected wards using ward-level estimates of the under-five population (Tables 2 and 3). This ensured that wards with larger under-five populations contributed proportionately more respondents to the study. Stage 2 Within each selected ward, communities were selected using simple random sampling. In some wards, more than one community was selected to ensure that the allocated sample size for that ward was achieved. Overall, in some wards, more than one community was selected to ensure that the allocated sample size was achieved, depending on population size and distribution of eligible households. Stage 3 A household listing was conducted in selected communities. Households were selected using systematic sampling. A random starting point was selected within each community, after which every second household was visited until the allocated sample size for each area was achieved. This approach was adopted due to the absence of a complete household sampling frame in the study areas. Stage 4 One eligible caregiver of a child under five years was selected per household. In households with more than one eligible caregiver, simple random selection was used. Where two eligible caregivers were present, selection was done by tossing a coin, while balloting was used where more than two eligible caregivers were present. No non-response was recorded among eligible caregivers approached, and the final analytic sample comprised 368 caregivers. 3.3.5 Data collection Quantitative data were collected using a structured interviewer-administered questionnaire developed by the authors based on a review of relevant literature on vaccine hesitancy. The questionnaire included items assessing caregivers’ knowledge, attitudes, healthcare service-related factors, and socio-cultural influences on vaccination. 3.3.6 Validity and reliability The instrument was pretested among caregivers in a non-selected LGA. Internal consistency was assessed using Cronbach’s alpha, yielding a coefficient of 0.78. Face and content validity were ensured through expert review by public health professionals. 3.3.7 Data analysis Quantitative data were analyzed using IBM SPSS version 27. Descriptive statistics were summarized using frequencies and percentages. Associations between variables were assessed using chi-square tests, while binary logistic regression was performed to identify predictors of vaccine hesitancy. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. There were no missing data in the final analytic dataset, as all 368 completed questionnaires were fully answered. In the event of item non-response during data collection, field supervisors revisited the respondent to obtain complete information. The analysis did not adjust for clustering at the ward or community level, which may lead to underestimated standard errors. 3.3.8 Operationalization of vaccine hesitancy Vaccine hesitancy was operationalized using two items adapted from the WHO Strategic Advisory Group of Experts (SAGE) Working Group on Vaccine Hesitancy definition: “delay in acceptance or refusal of vaccines despite availability of vaccination services” [2]. Caregivers were asked: (1) “Have you ever delayed your child’s measles vaccination?” and (2) “Have you ever refused a measles vaccine for your child?” Response options were Yes/No. A caregiver was classified as vaccine hesitant if they responded “Yes” to either question, indicating behavioral delay or refusal. Caregivers who responded “No” to both were classified as not hesitant. A binary vaccine hesitancy variable was then created, where caregivers who reported either refusing or delaying a measles vaccine were classified as vaccine hesitant (coded as 1), while those who reported neither behaviour were classified as non-hesitant (coded as 0). The quantitative analysis revealed a 44.6% prevalence of vaccine hesitancy, with younger caregivers more likely to be hesitant, while knowledge and attitude were not significant predictors. elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform targeted interventions to address structural, community, and interpersonal factors contributing to measles vaccine hesitancy, particularly in regions with relatively strong immunization infrastructure but persistent immunity gaps.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is context specific, and the achieved sample size of 368 would still provide adequate power (≥ 80%) to detect an odds ratio of 1.5 or greater for key predictors, assuming a design effect of up to 2.0. analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is context specific, and the achieved sample size of 368 would still provide adequate power (≥ 80%) to detect an odds ratio of 1.5 or greater for key predictors, assuming a design effect of up to 2.0. papers.full_text: 269 Measles is an acute infectious disease caused by measles virus infection, the main symptoms being fever, rash, and catarrhal symptoms. The measles virus is extremely contagious. Measles can be transmitted not only by droplet or contact infection but also by airborne transmission. As the measles virus also infects immune cells, it suppresses the immune system of infected individuals and causes various complications. Complications in the respiratory tract (pneumonia, laryngotracheobronchitis) and gastrointestinal tract (diarrhea, stomatitis), as well as otitis media, are frequent. Neurological complications are less common but often more severe, and include measles encephalitis, which appears within about two weeks of infection (approximately 1 case per 1,000 measles cases), and subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE), which has a poor prognosis and appears several years to more than a decade after infection and recovery (approximately 1 case per tens of thousands of measles cases). The World Health Organization (WHO) reports that an estimated 95,000 persons died from measles in 2024, with the majority being children under five years of age (https:// www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/measles). On the other hand, WHO considers measles to be an infectious disease that can be eliminated, because a safe and effective vaccine is available, subclinical infections are rare, accurate diagnostic methods are available, and humans are the only natural host; thus, WHO aims to eliminate measles. In 2005, the Regional Committee of the WHO Western Pacific Region (WPR), to which Japan belongs, resolved to eliminate measles from the WPR by 2012. In response to this, Japan introduced a two-dose measles-containing vaccine vaccination schedule (1st dose stage and 2nd dose stage) in 2006. Furthermore, in December 2007, the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW) issued the “Guidelines on Prevention of Specified Infectious Diseases: Measles” (latest revision in April 2019, hereinafter referred to as the “Guidelines”), and to strengthen the immunity of teenagers, who were the primary demographic affected in domestic outbreaks at the time, measures to eliminate measles were strengthened, including the implementation of a five-year (fiscal years [FY] 2008–2012) supplementary vaccination program for those of an age equivalent to the first year of junior high school (3rd round) and third year of senior high school (4th round) as routine vaccination under the Immunization Act. These measures led to a substantial decrease in measles cases in Japan from 2009, and in 2015, Japan was verified as having eliminated measles by the Regional Verification Commission for Measles Elimination in the WPR. Maintenance of elimination status has been verified through 2024, and documents to be submitted to the Commission regarding the status in 2025 are currently being compiled. Measles notification under the National Epidemiological Surveillance of Infectious Diseases: Measles is a Category V Infectious Disease under the Infectious Diseases Control Law (for notification criteria and disease classification, see https://www.mhlw.go.jp/ bunya/kenkou/kekkaku-kansenshou11/01-05-14-03. html). In 2008, when measles became a notifiable disease, there were 11,013 cases notified. Thereafter, the annual number of notified cases ranged from 35 to 744 through 2019, while the annual number was 10 or fewer during 2020–2022, when various measures, including travel restrictions, were implemented in response to the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic. Following the complete lifting of border control measures for COVID-19 in 2023, the annual number of notified cases increased to 28 in 2023 and 45 in 2024, and increased substantially to 265 in 2025 (Fig. 1). In terms of disease classification for the 265 case- patients reported in 2025, 62 of the 265 were modified measles, which are atypical laboratory-confirmed cases with only one or two of the three main symptoms (fever, rash, and catarrhal symptoms). Regarding age distribution, patients aged 20 years or older accounted for at least 60% of cases, with particularly large numbers of cases among those in their 20s and 30s (Fig. 2). As for vaccination history, 77 cases had no vaccination, 46 had received one dose, 52 had received two doses, and the vaccination history was unknown for 90 cases; 23 cases were aged less than 1 year and had not yet reached the age for routine vaccination (Table 1). It should be noted that, because the number of unvaccinated persons in the population is considered to be small, caution is required when comparing the number of cases among vaccinated and unvaccinated persons. Specimens for IgM antibody testing are sent from medical institutions to private laboratories, and specimens for genetic testing are sent from medical institutions primarily to public health institutes (PHIs) for testing. In 2025, all 265 cases were reported as laboratory-diagnosed cases. The Guidelines recommend performing the real-time RT-PCR test for detecting the viral gene, and, for specimens with positive results, analyzing the 450-base genotyping region of the measles virus N gene. Detection of measles virus (Infectious Agents Surveillance System): Among the 194 cases in which viral genes were detected at PHIs in 2025 and reported to the Infectious Agents Surveillance System of the National Epidemiological Surveillance of Infectious Diseases system, the viral genotype was B3 in 163 cases and D8 in 23 cases, while in 8 cases viral genes were detected but the nucleotide sequence could not be determined (Table 2). Among the 194 cases, 66 had a history of overseas travel and were suspected to have been infected overseas, while domestic infection was suspected in at least 60%. Among cases with a travel history, 51 had a history of travel to Vietnam, accounting for a large proportion (Table 2). Vaccination coverage: Since FY2006, routine measles vaccination has been implemented for children aged 1 year (the 1st dose stage) and for children in the year prior to entering elementary school (the 2nd dose stage). In FY2024, vaccination coverage was 92.7% for the 1st dose stage and 91.0% for the 2nd dose stage, both below the target coverage of 95% (https://www. mhlw.go.jp/bunya/kenkou/kekkaku-kansenshou21/ hashika.html). Also, the vaccination coverage for both the 1st and 2nd dose stages was the lowest in the past 10 years. National Epidemiological Surveillance of Vaccine- Preventable Diseases (NESVPD): In FY2025, measles antibody titers were measured by enzyme immunoassay (EIA) at PHIs in 20 prefectures under the NESVPD. The overall proportion positive for measles EIA antibody titers ≥2 was 96.1%, exceeding the 95% threshold required to prevent an epidemic (Fig. 4). Further measures to be taken: The number of reported measles cases globally, which was approximately 540,000 in 2019, decreased substantially to fewer than 100,000 in both 2020 and 2021 during the COVID-19 pandemic. However, it has remained above 100,000 since 2022, with approximately 280,000 cases reported in 2025, and outbreaks continue in many countries. In Japan, where measles elimination status has been achieved, measles occurrence often begins with cases imported from overseas. In 2025, there was a record-high number of approximately 42.68 million inbound visitors to Japan, and, representing an increase of 15.8% from 2024, the number of Japanese outbound travelers reached approximately 14.73 million (https:// statistics.jnto.go.jp/graph/#graph--inbound--travelers- -transition). Such indications of increasing movement of people between Japan and other countries are considered a factor that further increases the risk of measles occurrence. In 2025, there were also many cases for which the presumed place of infection was considered to be within Japan, underscoring the need to establish an environment in which infection does not spread domestically even when measles virus is imported from overseas. To achieve this goal, as outlined in the Guidelines, the following efforts are important: 1) achieve and maintain vaccination coverage of at least 95% for the two routine doses; 2) maintain a surveillance system based on rapid Table 2. In particular, routine vaccination coverage in FY2024 did not reach the target of 95% for either the 1st or 2nd dose stage, and efforts to improve routine vaccination coverage are considered an important challenge. In addition, imported measles may be brought into Japan not only by inbound visitors but also by residents of Japan after traveling to countries where measles is circulating; therefore, measures such as raising awareness among travelers are also important. In recent years, the presumed countries of infection among imported cases have tended to be Southeast Asian countries, including Vietnam, and continued awareness-raising among travelers to these areas remains important. In addition, in 2025, measles resurged in countries that had previously achieved measles elimination, including Canada and the United Kingdom, resulting in revocation of their elimination status; therefore, raising awareness among travelers to these countries with measles resurgence is also important. Furthermore, because more than 500 measles cases have been confirmed in Japan from January through the end of May 2026, it is necessary to further strengthen collaborative approaches, including information sharing among local governments, MHLW, Japan Institute for Health Security (JIHS), and other relevant organizations, in order to monitor the domestic epidemiologic situation and prevent widespread transmission. Landeta-Sa, Departamento de Dermatología y Micología, Hospital General de México Dr. Eduardo Liceaga, Ciudad de México, México Ana C. Carbajal-César, Departamento de Pediatría y Epidemiología Clínica, Instituto Nacional de Pediatría, Ciudad de México, México Alejandra M. Guerrero-Villalpando, Departamento de Cardiopatías Congénitas y Pediatría, Instituto Nacional de Cardiología Ignacio Chávez, Ciudad de México, México Mariana Vélez-Pintado, Departamento de Medicina Interna e Infectología, Centro Médico ABC, Ciudad de México, México Measles is a highly contagious, vaccine-preventable viral disease of mandatory epidemiological reporting that remains an active global public health threat. Caused by the measles virus (Paramyxoviridae family), a single-serotype pathogen with a basic reproduction number of 12-18, it is transmitted via aerosolized respiratory droplets. The classic clinical presentation begins with a prodrome of fever, cough, coryza, and conjunctivitis, followed by Koplik’s spots and a characteristic cephalocaudal maculopapular rash. Diagnosis is confirmed through specific IgM serology, polymerase chain reaction or viral culture. Management is primarily supportive; vitamin A supplementation reduces childhood mortality by up to 62% and is universally recommended by the WHO for all diagnosed children. Complications occur in approximately 30% of cases; the most frequent and usually mild include diarrhea (8%) and otitis media (7-9%), while severe complications include pneumonia, diarrhea, acute encephalitis, acute post-infectious measles encephalomyelitis, and, years later, subacute sclerosing panencephalitis. The most vulnerable populations include children under 5, young adults without prior immunization, pregnant women, and immunocompromised individuals. The MMR vaccine (measles, mumps and rubella) achieves 97% efficacy after two doses and requires population coverage above 93% to sustain herd immunity. In Mexico, declining vaccination rates contributed to more than 12,000 confirmed cases and over 33 deaths accumulated during the 2025–2026 outbreak, predominantly in unvaccinated children. Post-exposure prophylaxis with MMR within 72 hours or immunoglobulin within 6 days is indicated for susceptible high-risk individuals. Global coordination, sustained vaccination campaigns, and heightened clinical awareness remain essential to curb transmission. This article was prepared to provide a comprehensive review of measles, covering the associated risks, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention. Keywords: Vaccines. Febrile exanthem. Herd immunity. Outbreak. Paramyxoviridae.

analysis.scope_and_question: Measles virus (Morbillivirus hominis), historical taxonomic names, rubeola and measles disease. The review focuses on the epidemiology, clinical presentation, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of measles virus infections, with an emphasis on public health implications and the role of vaccination in controlling outbreaks.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is based on a comprehensive analysis of literature, including clinical studies, epidemiological reports, and public health guidelines. It includes evidence from multiple sources, such as WHO recommendations, clinical case studies, and outbreak data. The review does not explicitly report on meta-analysis or pooled estimates but synthesizes findings from various studies to form a coherent overview of measles virus-related topics.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Measles is a highly contagious, vaccine-preventable viral disease caused by the measles virus, with a basic reproduction number of 12-18. It is transmitted via aerosolized respiratory droplets and presents with a characteristic prodrome followed by a maculopapular rash. Vitamin A supplementation is universally recommended for all diagnosed children, reducing childhood mortality by up to 62%. The MMR vaccine achieves 97% efficacy after two doses and requires population coverage above 93% to sustain herd immunity. Complications occur in approximately 30% of cases, with severe outcomes including pneumonia, acute encephalitis, and subacute sclerosing panencephalitis.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights the importance of maintaining high vaccination rates to prevent outbreaks, but it does not provide specific data on the effectiveness of different vaccination strategies in diverse populations. There is also a lack of detailed information on the long-term effects of measles virus infections and the potential for resurgence in regions with low vaccination coverage. Additionally, the review does not address the role of specific measles virus genotypes in disease severity or transmission dynamics.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Global coordination, sustained vaccination campaigns, and heightened clinical awareness are essential to curb measles transmission. Research should focus on improving vaccination strategies, particularly in vulnerable populations such as children under 5, young adults without prior immunization, pregnant women, and immunocompromised individuals. Surveillance and diagnostic methods should be enhanced to ensure timely identification and management of measles cases. Post-exposure prophylaxis with MMR vaccine within 72 hours or immunoglobulin within 6 days is recommended for high-risk individuals.

analysis.summary_en: This review provides an overview of measles virus, emphasizing its epidemiology, clinical presentation, and public health significance. It highlights the importance of vaccination in preventing outbreaks and reducing mortality, particularly through vitamin A supplementation. The review underscores the need for global coordination and sustained vaccination efforts to maintain herd immunity. However, it notes gaps in understanding the long-term effects of measles infections and the role of specific genotypes in disease outcomes. Research and practice implications include improving vaccination strategies, enhancing surveillance, and ensuring timely post-exposure prophylaxis for high-risk groups.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 麻疹病毒(人麻疹病毒),历史分类学名称,风疹和 麻疹 疾病。该综述的重点是 流行病学、临床表现、诊断、治疗 和 麻疹病毒 感染的预防,重点是公共卫生影响和 疫苗接种 在控制 暴发 中的作用。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该审查基于对文献的综合分析,包括临床研究、流行病学报告和公共卫生指南。它包括来自多个来源的证据,例如 WHO 建议、临床案例研究和 暴发 数据。该综述没有明确报告荟萃分析或汇总估计,而是综合了各种研究的结果,以形成 麻疹病毒 相关主题的连贯概述。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 麻疹 是一种由 麻疹病毒 引起的高度传染性、疫苗 可预防的病毒性疾病,基本繁殖数为 12-18。它通过雾化呼吸道飞沫传播,并出现典型的前驱症状,随后出现斑丘疹。普遍建议所有确诊儿童补充维生素 A,使儿童 死亡率 减少高达 62%。MMR 疫苗 在两次接种后达到 97% 的功效,并需要 93% 以上的人群覆盖率才能维持群体免疫。大约 30% 的病例会出现并发症,严重后果包括肺炎、急性脑炎和 亚急性硬化性全脑炎。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述强调了维持高 疫苗接种 率对于预防 疫苗接种 的重要性,但它没有提供不同 疫苗接种 策略在不同人群中有效性的具体数据。还缺乏关于 麻疹病毒 感染的长期影响以及在 麻疹病毒 覆盖率低的地区重新流行的可能性的详细信息。此外,该综述没有讨论特定 麻疹病毒 基因型在疾病严重程度或 传播 动态中的作用。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 全球协调、持续的 疫苗接种 活动以及提高临床意识对于遏制 麻疹 传播 至关重要。研究应侧重于改进 疫苗接种 策略,特别是针对 5 岁以下儿童、未事先免疫的年轻人、孕妇和免疫功能低下个体等弱势群体。应加强麻疹和诊断方法,确保及时识别和管理麻疹病例。建议高危个体在 72 小时内使用 MMR 疫苗 或在 6 天内使用免疫球蛋白进行暴露后预防。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 麻疹病毒(人麻疹病毒),历史分类学名称,风疹和 麻疹 疾病。该综述的重点是 流行病学、临床表现、诊断、治疗 和 麻疹病毒 感染的预防,重点是公共卫生影响和 疫苗接种 在控制 暴发 中的作用。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该审查基于对文献的综合分析,包括临床研究、流行病学报告和公共卫生指南。它包括来自多个来源的证据,例如 WHO 建议、临床案例研究和 暴发 数据。该综述没有明确报告荟萃分析或汇总估计,而是综合了各种研究的结果,以形成 麻疹病毒 相关主题的连贯概述。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 麻疹 是一种由 麻疹病毒 引起的高度传染性、疫苗 可预防的病毒性疾病,基本繁殖数为 12-18。它通过雾化呼吸道飞沫传播,并出现典型的前驱症状,随后出现斑丘疹。普遍建议所有确诊儿童补充维生素 A,使儿童 死亡率 减少高达 62%。MMR 疫苗 在两次接种后达到 97% 的功效,并需要 93% 以上的人群覆盖率才能维持群体免疫。大约 30% 的病例会出现并发症,严重后果包括肺炎、急性脑炎和 亚急性硬化性全脑炎。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述强调了维持高 疫苗接种 率对于预防 疫苗接种 的重要性,但它没有提供不同 疫苗接种 策略在不同人群中有效性的具体数据。还缺乏关于 麻疹病毒 感染的长期影响以及在 麻疹病毒 覆盖率低的地区重新流行的可能性的详细信息。此外,该综述没有讨论特定 麻疹病毒 基因型在疾病严重程度或 传播 动态中的作用。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 全球协调、持续的 疫苗接种 活动以及提高临床意识对于遏制 麻疹 传播 至关重要。研究应侧重于改进 疫苗接种 策略,特别是针对 5 岁以下儿童、未事先免疫的年轻人、孕妇和免疫功能低下个体等弱势群体。应加强麻疹和诊断方法,确保及时识别和管理麻疹病例。建议高危个体在 72 小时内使用 MMR 疫苗 或在 6 天内使用免疫球蛋白进行暴露后预防。

papers.title: Transmission‐Based Infection Control Preparedness in Dentistry: Lessons From Andes Virus, Measles, and Ebola Epidemics
papers.abstract: A critical, annotated version of Narlikar’s iconic novel about a cybervirus attack by an advanced alien species—with updated text and added material. A year before Robin Cook’s Invasion (1997)—in which an alien force activates a latent biological virus in humans—and almost a decade before Liu Cixin’s The Remembrance of Earth’s Past trilogy (2008–2010)—in which humanity’s scientific progress is curtailed by an alien supercomputer’s “sophon-lock”—Jayant Vishnu Narlikar’s Virus (1996) painted a similar scenario. In his novel, a cybervirus broadcast by an advanced, extraterrestrial species invades Earth and freezes its digital infrastructure: a prelude to an alien invasion. The novel, first published in Marathi, recounts how vast radio arrays on Earth intercept a seemingly innocuous message from an unknown planet orbiting Barnard’s Star. The radio signal, sent six years prior, coalesces into a cybervirus that has the potential to cause a complete digital meltdown and lead humanity into an age of chaos—an alien first strike to prevent humanity from evolving further. This book—a critical, annotated version of Virus, edited and revised by Sami Ahmad Khan—reissues Narlikar’s iconic novel with updated text and added dimensions. It includes detailed annotations that locate the technology of the text along the axis of contemporary scientific thought, as well as critical essays that focus on the literary, political, and sociocultural dimensions of the novel; essays on Narlikar’s role in India’s science and science fiction; an exclusive conversation with the author; bibliographical information on his works; and a bonus short story. Contributions by Sami Ahmad Khan, Nilam Ingole, Priteegandha Naik, Jayant V. Narlikar, and Dibyadyuti Roy.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore preparedness for transmission-based infection control in dentistry by drawing lessons from the Andes virus, measles, and Ebola epidemics. The background highlights the historical context of these viral outbreaks and their implications for public health.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study design involved a review of existing literature and case studies from the Andes virus, measles, and Ebola epidemics, focusing on transmission-based infection control measures.
analysis.methods: The methods included a comprehensive review of the literature, analysis of case studies, and identification of key lessons for improving infection control in dental settings.
analysis.main_results: The study found that lessons from the Andes virus, measles, and Ebola epidemics could be applied to enhance transmission-based infection control in dentistry, emphasizing the importance of strict hygiene protocols, personal protective equipment, and rapid response systems.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as novel insights into the application of historical epidemic lessons to modern dental practice, highlighting the need for continuous improvement in infection control measures.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings could inform the development of more robust infection control protocols in dental settings, potentially reducing the risk of transmission of infectious diseases.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the reliance on historical case studies and the potential for bias in the interpretation of lessons learned. The evidence strength is moderate due to the observational nature of the study.

analysis.summary_en: This study reviewed lessons from the Andes virus, measles, and Ebola epidemics to enhance transmission-based infection control in dentistry, emphasizing the need for strict hygiene protocols and rapid response systems.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 研究设计回顾了安第斯病毒、麻疹 和埃博拉疫情的现有文献和案例研究,重点关注基于 传播 的感染控制措施。
elements_zh.methods: 这些方法包括全面回顾文献、分析案例研究以及确定改善牙科环境感染控制的关键经验教训。
elements_zh.main_results: 研究发现,安第斯病毒、麻疹 和埃博拉疫情的经验教训可用于加强基于 传播 的牙科感染控制,强调严格的卫生规程、个人防护设备和快速反应系统的重要性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为将历史流行病教训应用​​于现代牙科实践的新颖见解,强调了不断改进感染控制措施的必要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为牙科环境中制定更强大的感染控制方案提供信息,从而有可能降低 传播 传染病的风险。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性包括依赖历史案例研究以及对经验教训的解释可能存在偏见。由于该研究的观察性质,证据强度中等。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在通过吸取安第斯病毒、麻疹 和埃博拉疫情的经验教训,探索牙科中基于 传播 的感染控制的准备情况。背景突出了这些病毒 暴发 的历史背景及其对公共卫生的影响。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 研究设计回顾了安第斯病毒、麻疹 和埃博拉疫情的现有文献和案例研究,重点关注基于 传播 的感染控制措施。
analysis_zh.methods: 这些方法包括全面回顾文献、分析案例研究以及确定改善牙科环境感染控制的关键经验教训。
analysis_zh.main_results: 研究发现,安第斯病毒、麻疹 和埃博拉疫情的经验教训可用于加强基于 传播 的牙科感染控制,强调严格的卫生规程、个人防护设备和快速反应系统的重要性。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为将历史流行病教训应用​​于现代牙科实践的新颖见解,强调了不断改进感染控制措施的必要性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为牙科环境中制定更强大的感染控制方案提供信息,从而有可能降低 传播 传染病的风险。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性包括依赖历史案例研究以及对经验教训的解释可能存在偏见。由于该研究的观察性质,证据强度中等。

papers.full_text: The United States has lost its measles elimination status – an international designation reflecting an absence of local measles transmission for at least 12 months – a public health achievement held since 2000. A commission of the Pan American Health Organization, a regional office of the World Health Organization that oversees the Americas, reached that conclusion in November 2026, with a formal announcement expected Nov. 17. Canada lost its measles elimination status in 2025, as did the United Kingdom and other countries in Europe and central Asia in early 2026. These losses of status are no mystery. Measles is one of the most contagious diseases and still circulates in much of the world. What keeps the disease in check is herd immunity – when a high enough percentage of the population is vaccinated to break the chains of transmission. For measles, that’s at least 95%. But in 2025-26, only 92% of kindergartners in the U.S. received the measles, mumps and rubella, or MMR, vaccine. I’m an epidemiologist who studies misinformation in the same way others study smoking or air pollution: as an exposure that makes populations sick. For years I’ve watched vaccine misinformation help erode the coverage that kept measles from spreading. An effective vaccine A measles vaccine has existed in the U.S. since 1963. The combined MMR vaccine followed in 1971; two doses are about 97% effective. A federal program created in 1993 made it free for eligible children. After widespread vaccination efforts, reported cases dropped more than 99%, and by 2000 measles was declared eliminated. But due to the success of the MMR vaccine, within a generation most parents and many doctors had never even seen a measles case. The experts who certified elimination in 2000 warned that maintaining elimination status would require sustained high rates of vaccination, fast outbreak response and strong surveillance. Drop any one of these conditions and imported cases would spread. So how does a country with a 97% effective vaccine lose measles elimination status? One obvious explanation: The vaccine worked so well that people forgot what the disease does. Before the vaccine, measles infected 3 million to 4 million Americans a year. Tens of thousands were hospitalized, and hundreds died. Parents didn’t need convincing. They had seen it. Even with most cases unreported, the official count in 1963 was nearly 400,000 cases. About 1 in 20 children who contract measles develop pneumonia. The virus can also erase part of the immune system’s memory, an effect called immune amnesia, leaving children open to infections they had already beaten. In rare cases, it causes a fatal brain disease, subacute sclerosing panencephalitis, which appears years after apparent recovery. In 2025, a child in Los Angeles died of it. A surge of outbreaks – and deaths As of Nov. 12, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention counted 5,412 cases for 2026 – the highest number since 1991 – and 591 hospitalizations. Among children under 5, 1 in 6 have been hospitalized. Six deaths appear in the CDC’s 2026 count, which now relies on federal death certificate data. States, using a broader definition, report a total of 10 deaths: seven in Pennsylvania, one in New York and two in Wisconsin. Pennsylvania’s outbreak alone has produced 1,542 cases and 305 hospitalizations, by the state’s Nov. 13 count. Major outbreaks have also hit South Carolina, Utah and Arizona since the West Texas outbreak of early 2025, which was the start of the national surge of measles outbreaks. Utah’s outbreak, which began in June 2025, has gone well past the 12-month mark. That outbreak alone breaches the WHO’s definition of measles elimination and could have triggered the loss of elimination status. Fertile ground for misinformation When no one remembers the disease, the vaccine becomes the only thing left to fear. Misinformation feeds on that imbalance. Parents who had never seen measles had nothing vivid to weigh against claims of vaccine risk, so even discredited risks felt plausible. A 1998 paper fraudulently linking MMR to autism was retracted in 2010, and its author lost his medical license. But the damage was already done, and this myth persists to this day, even though studies that included millions of children have found no link. During the COVID-19 pandemic, vaccine misinformation proliferated in echo chambers on social media. It is no surprise that the percentage of kindergartners who have received their MMR shots has fallen every year since the 2019-20 school year. In a 2025 KFF poll, parents who believed any false measles claim were more than twice as likely to have skipped or delayed vaccines. Since the COVID-19 pandemic, the anti-vaccine movement has also used the banner of medical freedom to gain a larger, more mainstream audience. Federal policy fuels further confusion Now these arguments have found an audience in federal policy. On Aug. 10, 2026, President Donald Trump signed an order calling for MMR to be split into three single-disease shots, which are not sold in the United States. There is no published evidence that separating MMR offers any benefit, and more doctor visits mean more chances for missed doses. Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. suggested in August that Pennsylvania’s first two measles-associated deaths “may even have been altogether fabricated.” State officials had investigated both. While questioning the vaccine and measles deaths, he has promoted vitamin A and nutrition as measles cures. The CDC classifies vitamin A as a supportive treatment, not a cure or vaccine substitute. Vaccination rates for the MMR vaccine among U.S. kindergartners fell from 95.2% in 2019-20 to 92.4% in 2025-26. Exemptions from any required vaccine rose to a record 4.2%. Of this year’s cases, 96% were unvaccinated or of unknown status. The 92.4% kindergarten vaccination rate leaves about 280,000 kindergartners without documented MMR. Among states, Idaho has the lowest MMR rate with 75.2% among Idaho kindergartners, while some counties and communities there and elsewhere have even lower rates. Adult immunity also has gaps: Adults are 41% of this year’s cases, and 15% of them were hospitalized. Many who were vaccinated before 1989, when a second MMR dose was added, got only one. Roadblocks to recovery Regaining elimination status means the U.S experiencing at least 12 months without continuous transmission. That will require the same factors that led to the U.S. earning that status in 2000: stronger surveillance, speedy outbreak response and increased vaccination rates. But it will also require federal health leadership that is focused on bringing those things about. The Department of Health and Human Services blames current vaccination gaps on missed pediatrician appointments during the COVID-19 pandemic. CDC Director Erica Schwartz said that the agency would not make any changes in measles response efforts in light of losing elimination status. Additionally, orders like August’s about the MMR vaccine, and revisions to long-standing vaccine recommendations, are weakening vaccination efforts. Also, on top of a chronically underfunded public health infrastructure , many career public health scientists lost their jobs in 2025. The surveillance capacity that made elimination possible has been substantially weakened. So what does this mean for Americans? The loss of measles elimination status in the U.S. does not change the fact that the vaccine is safe and effective – and it is now more important than ever.

I’m an epidemiologist who studies misinformation in the same way others study smoking or air pollution: as an exposure that makes populations sick. The United States has lost its measles elimination status – an international designation reflecting an absence of local measles transmission for at least 12 months – a public health achievement held since 2000. Canada lost its measles elimination status in 2025, as did the United Kingdom and other countries in Europe and central Asia in early 2026. These losses of status are no mystery. Measles is one of the most contagious diseases and still circulates in much of the world. What keeps the disease in check is herd immunity – when a high enough percentage of the population is vaccinated to break the chains of transmission. For measles, that’s at least 95%. But in 2025-26, only 92% of kindergartners in the U.S. received the measles, mumps and rubella, or MMR, vaccine. For years I’ve watched vaccine misinformation help erode the coverage that kept measles from spreading. An effective vaccine A measles vaccine has existed in the U.S. The combined MMR vaccine followed in 1971; two doses are about 97% effective. A federal program created in 1993 made it free for eligible children. After widespread vaccination efforts, reported cases dropped more than 99%, and by 2000 measles was declared eliminated. papers.title: Perfil epidemiológico da reemergência do sarampo no Brasil (2015-2025)
papers.abstract: Objective: To analyze the epidemiological profile of measles re-emergence in Brazil between 2015 and 2025, considering incidence, mortality, vaccination coverage, and regional and demographic distribution. Methods: A retrospective, descriptive, ecological time-series study using DATASUS data. Incidence, mortality, vaccination coverage, and epidemiological profiles were analyzed according to demographic and regional variables using descriptive statistics, Prais-Winsten regression, Spearman correlation, and comparisons between epidemiological phases. Results: A resurgence in incidence occurred starting in 2018, peaking at 10.47 cases per 100,000 inhabitants in 2019. Phase 2 (2018–2020) saw the highest incidence rates, marking the primary critical period of re-emergence. A heterogeneous distribution was observed, with greater vulnerability in the North region, higher occurrence among children aged 0 to 4 years, and a concentration of deaths between 2018 and 2021. Vaccination coverage showed a downward trend for both the first and second doses of the MMR (measles, mumps, and rubella) and MMRV (measles, mumps, rubella, and varicella) vaccines. The correlation between vaccination coverage and incidence was negative but not statistically significant. Conclusion: The findings demonstrated a temporal coexistence between declining vaccination coverage and the resurgence of measles incidence, within a context of regional heterogeneity and persistent epidemiological conditions favorable to new outbreaks.
authors: Laís Valentina Resnauer Taques da Silva Dias

papers.title: District immunization coverage before, during and after the 2023 big catch-up in Sierra Leone: an ecological analysis of routine administrative data and population denominators, 2020 to 2025
papers.abstract: Administrative coverage is recorded vaccinations divided by the estimated eligible population and exceeds 100% when recorded doses exceed the estimate. We examined reported coverage across Sierra Leone’s 16 districts before, during and after the 2023 Big Catch-Up, and how the denominators affected the results. This ecological analysis used 1,536 district and 96 national DHIS2 records for 16 indicators, 2020 to 2025. District-clustered Poisson generalized estimating equations compared 2023 with 2020 to 2022, and 2024 to 2025 with 2023. Between-district differences in fully immunized child and measles second-dose coverage were measured with the standard deviation and population-weighted Gini coefficient (bootstrap intervals), under alternative denominators and capping at 100%, and with ratios between recorded dose counts. National fully immunized child coverage rose from 86.5% (2020 to 2022) to 106.4% in 2023 (rate ratio 1.23, 95% confidence interval 1.12 to 1.36) and was 108.1% in 2025. The lowest district value rose from 67.3% in 2022 to 84.9% in 2025; the four lowest districts of 2020 to 2022 later reported 110% to 121%. The Gini coefficient for coverage as reported changed by + 0.013 from 2022 to 2025 (95% bootstrap interval − 0.027 to 0.044); with coverage capped at 100%, it fell from 0.067 to 0.025. District coverage changes from 2023 to 2025 correlated with projection changes (rho − 0.67). The fully immunized child count exceeded its smallest component dose count in 54 of 96 district-years. The measles second-to-first dose ratio was 0.79 in 2022, 0.93 in 2023 and 0.84 in 2025. The 2023 Big Catch-Up was associated with increased recorded immunization activity across Sierra Leone, and recorded counts remained above 2023 levels through 2025 for all indicators except measles second dose. However, whether variation between districts widened or narrowed depended on how coverage above 100% was treated, and post-catch-up coverage changes were closely linked to revisions of the population projections. Administrative coverage should therefore be interpreted alongside recorded counts and dose-completion ratios, while strengthening routine measles second-dose and birth-dose vaccination remains a priority.
papers.journal: International Journal for Equity in Health

Between-district differences in fully immunized child and measles second-dose coverage were measured with the standard deviation and population-weighted Gini coefficient (bootstrap intervals), under alternative denominators and capping at 100%, and with ratios between recorded dose counts. National fully immunized child coverage rose from 86.5% (2020 to 2022) to 106.4% in 2023 (rate ratio 1.23, 95% confidence interval 1.12 to 1.36) and was 108.1% in 2025. The lowest district value rose from 67.3% in 2022 to 84.9% in 2025; the four lowest districts of 2020 to 2022 later reported 110% to 121%. The Gini coefficient for coverage as reported changed by + 0.013 from 2022 to 2025 (95% bootstrap interval − 0.027 to 0.044); with coverage capped at 100%, it fell from 0.067 to 0.025. District coverage changes from 2023 to 2025 correlated with projection changes (rho − 0.67). The fully immunized child count exceeded its smallest component dose count in 54 of 96 district-years. The measles second-to-first dose ratio was 0.79 in 2022, 0.93 in 2023 and 0.84 in 2025. The 2023 Big Catch-Up was associated with increased recorded immunization activity across Sierra Leone, and recorded counts remained above 2023 levels through 2025 for all indicators except measles second dose. However, whether variation between districts widened or narrowed depended on how coverage above 100% was treated, and post-catch-up coverage changes were closely linked to revisions of the population projections. Administrative coverage should therefore be interpreted alongside recorded counts and dose-completion ratios, while strengthening routine measles second-dose and birth-dose vaccination remains a priority.

papers.title: Childhood Vaccination Coverage and Adult Immunization Policy: An Exploratory Comparison of Egypt, Canada, and the United States
papers.abstract: Introduction Childhood immunization coverage is measured in a comparatively standardized way, whereas adult vaccination is documented through four distinct dimensions: recommendation, program availability, uptake, and dose distribution. This study compared childhood coverage rankings with the documented dimensions of adult vaccination policy in three deliberately contrasting countries to examine whether they aligned. The comparison was descriptive and was not intended to test predictive relationships or establish statistical association. Methods We analyzed a fixed extraction of the 2024 revision of the WHO/UNICEF Estimates of National Immunization Coverage (WUENIC) for diphtheria-tetanus-pertussis third-dose (DTP3) and measles-containing vaccine first-dose (MCV1) in Egypt, Canada, and the United States from 2015 to 2024. We calculated descriptive statistics and exploratory ordinary least-squares trends with Newey-West standard errors (lag 1). Sensitivity analyses used t-based intervals, conventional standard errors, and Holm adjustment for six tests. Adult evidence from official schedules, guidance, national surveys, and published Egyptian studies was organized qualitatively into four constructs: recommendation, availability, uptake, and distribution. Adult policy breadth was described, not scored. A post hoc analysis compared DTP3 trends for 2015-2024 with those for 2000-2024 in Egypt and Canada. Results Egypt had the highest mean WUENIC coverage for both DTP3 (95.2%) and MCV1 (94.9%), followed by the United States (94.1% and 91.6%) and Canada (91.5% and 90.4%). The official sources reviewed documented broader adult recommendation frameworks for Canada and the United States than for Egypt, where adult uptake had been measured only for COVID-19 and in healthcare workers. Adult uptake estimates were not comparable across the three countries. Egypt's DTP3 trend was +0.364 percentage points per year for 2015-2024 (95% CI 0.277 to 0.450) but -0.132 for 2000-2024 (95% CI -0.213 to -0.050), showing sensitivity to the time window. Conclusion Childhood coverage rankings did not align with the documented breadth of adult immunization policy. Because adult-policy documentation and uptake measurement differed substantially, these results cannot demonstrate an inverse relationship or rank the overall performance of national immunization systems. Childhood coverage and the four adult dimensions should be reported separately.

papers.abstract_zh: 简介 儿童免疫覆盖率以相对标准化的方式衡量,而成人 疫苗接种 通过四个不同的维度进行记录:推荐、计划可用性、吸收和剂量分布。这项研究将三个故意对比的国家的儿童覆盖率排名与成人 疫苗接种 政策的记录维度进行了比较,以检验它们是否一致。该比较是描述性的,并非旨在测试预测关系或建立统计关联。方法 我们分析了2015年至2024年埃及、加拿大和美国白喉-破伤风-百日咳第三剂(DTP3)和包含麻疹的疫苗第一剂(MCV1)的世界卫生组织/联合国儿童基金会国家免疫覆盖率估计值(WUENIC)2024年修订版的固定提取内容。我们计算了描述性统计数据以及带有 Newey-West 标准误差的探索性普通最小二乘趋势(滞后 1)。敏感性分析使用基于 t 的区间、传统标准误差和 Holm 调整进行六次检验。来自官方时间表、指南、全国调查和已发表的埃及研究的成人证据被定性地分为四个结构:推荐、可用性、吸收和分发。成人政策的广度是描述的,而不是评分的。事后分析将埃及和加拿大 2015-2024 年的 DTP3 趋势与 2000-2024 年的趋势进行了比较。结果 埃及的 DTP3 (95.2%) 和 MCV1 (94.9%) 平均 WUENIC 覆盖率最高,其次是美国(94.1% 和 91.6%)和加拿大(91.5% 和 90.4%)。官方消息来源审查了加拿大和美国比埃及更广泛的成人推荐框架,埃及仅测量了 COVID-19 和医护人员的成人吸收率。这三个国家的成人吸收率估计值不具有可比性。2015-2024 年埃及的 DTP3 趋势为每年+0.364 个百分点(95% CI 0.277 至 0.450),但 2000-2024 年为-0.132(95% CI -0.213 至 -0.050),显示出对时间窗口的敏感性。结论 儿童覆盖率排名与成人免疫政策记录的广度不一致。由于成人政策文件和吸收测量存在很大差异,这些结果无法证明反向关系或对国家免疫系统的整体绩效进行排名。儿童覆盖率和四个成人维度应单独报告。

papers.title: Timing of de novo vaccination during pregnancy impacts maternal and newborn immunity
papers.abstract: Maternal immunity is essential for protecting both the pregnant individual and fetus, balancing immune tolerance with defense against infection. While maternal vaccination enhances protection, the impact of gestational timing on antibody responses and transplacental antibody transfer remains unclear. The COVID-19 pandemic provided a unique opportunity to study primary SARS-CoV-2 vaccine-induced humoral responses in individuals without documented prior SARS-CoV-2 infection or vaccination. To investigate how vaccination timing shapes maternal and fetal immunity, we performed comprehensive serological profiling in 263 individuals, including 96 maternal–neonatal dyads, sampled across pregnancy and at delivery. Leveraging natural variation in SARS-CoV-2 vaccine timing, we assessed antibody responses to SARS-CoV-2 and 13 additional pathogens using Systems Serology, analyzing isotypes, subclasses, FcγR binding, glycosylation, neutralization, and Fc-mediated functions. Pregnant individuals maintained stable immunity to previously encountered antigens (from past infections or vaccinations) and mounted expected responses to pertussis and tetanus boosters. Initial responses to COVID-19 mRNA vaccination were attenuated in third-trimester vaccinees but reached comparable levels after the second dose. Enhanced responses to unrelated antigens, such as poliovirus and measles, were observed, particularly in later gestation, potentially due to cross-reactivity. Antibody transfer was most efficient following late second to early third trimester vaccination, with decreased transfer in the late third trimester. Fetal sex also influenced antibody transfer efficiency, favoring male fetuses in the third trimester. These findings underscore the importance of vaccine timing to optimize maternal and neonatal immunity.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how the timing of vaccination during pregnancy affects maternal and fetal immunity. The research focuses on antibody responses to SARS-CoV-2 and other pathogens, using Systems Serology to analyze various immune parameters. The main results show that antibody transfer is most efficient when vaccination occurs in the late second to early third trimester, with decreased transfer in the late third trimester. Fetal sex also influenced antibody transfer efficiency, with male fetuses showing higher transfer rates. The findings highlight the importance of vaccine timing to optimize immunity for both the mother and the newborn. The study's implications suggest that adjusting vaccination schedules during pregnancy could enhance protection for the fetus. The evidence is based on serological profiling of 263 individuals, including 96 maternal–neonatal dyads, and the results are interpreted within the context of immune responses. The study's design and methods are described, but no specific limitations are reported.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 为了研究 疫苗接种 时机如何影响母体和胎儿的免疫力,我们对 263 名个体(包括 96 名母婴二人组)进行了全面的血清学分析,在怀孕期间和分娩时进行了采样。
elements_zh.methods: 利用 SARS-CoV-2 疫苗 时间的自然变异,我们使用 Systems 血清学 评估了抗体对 SARS-CoV-2 和 13 种其他病原体的反应,分析同种型、亚类、FcγR 结合、糖基化、中和和 Fc 介导的功能。
elements_zh.main_results: 抗体转移在妊娠中期后期至妊娠晚期 疫苗接种 后最为有效,而在妊娠晚期则转移减少。胎儿性别也影响抗体转移效率,有利于妊娠晚期的男性胎儿。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现强调了 疫苗 时机对于优化孕产妇和新生儿免疫力的重要性。

papers.abstract_zh: 母体免疫力对于保护孕妇和胎儿、平衡免疫耐受与防御感染至关重要。虽然母体 疫苗接种 增强了保护,但妊娠时间对抗体反应和经胎盘抗体转移的影响仍不清楚。COVID-19 大流行提供了一个独特的机会,可以在没有记录的先前 SARS-CoV-2 感染或 疫苗 的个体中研究原发性 SARS-CoV-2 疫苗 诱导的体液反应。为了研究 疫苗接种 时机如何影响母体和胎儿的免疫力,我们对 263 名个体(包括 96 名母婴二人组)进行了全面的血清学分析,在怀孕期间和分娩时进行了采样。利用 SARS-CoV-2 疫苗 时间的自然变异,我们使用 Systems 血清学 评估了抗体对 SARS-CoV-2 和 13 种其他病原体的反应,分析同种型、亚类、FcγR 结合、糖基化、中和和 Fc 介导的功能。怀孕个体对先前遇到的抗原(来自过去的感染或疫苗接种)保持稳定的免疫力,并对百日咳和破伤风加强免疫产生预期的反应。对 COVID-19 mRNA 疫苗接种 的初始反应在妊娠晚期 疫苗 中减弱,但在第二次给药后达到了相当的水平。观察到对不相关抗原(例如脊髓灰质炎病毒和 麻疹)的反应增强,特别是在妊娠后期,可能是由于交叉反应。抗体转移在妊娠中期后期至妊娠晚期 疫苗接种 后最为有效,而在妊娠晚期则转移减少。胎儿性别也影响抗体转移效率,有利于妊娠晚期的男性胎儿。这些发现强调了 疫苗 时机对于优化孕产妇和新生儿免疫力的重要性。

papers.title: Sarampión: de la eliminación al rebrote. Revisión de la literatura y recomendaciones actuales
papers.abstract: El sarampión es una enfermedad viral altamente contagiosa, prevenible por vacunación y de notificación obligatoria, que representa un problema de salud pública vigente. Su agente causal es el virus del sarampión (familia Paramyxoviridae), de serotipo único, transmitido por vía aérea con un número reproductivo básico de 12 a 18. La presentación clínica clásica incluye un pródromo de fiebre, tos, coriza y conjuntivitis, seguido de las manchas de Koplik y un exantema maculopapular cefalocaudal. El diagnóstico se confirma mediante serología (IgM específica), reacción en cadena de la polimerasa o cultivo viral. El tratamiento es fundamentalmente de soporte; en pacientes pediátricos, la vitamina A reduce la mortalidad hasta un 62%, por lo que está recomendada por la OMS en este grupo de pacientes. Las complicaciones ocurren en aproximadamente el 30% de los casos; las más frecuentes son diarrea (8%) y otitis media (7-9%), y las complicaciones graves incluyen neumonía, diarrea, encefalitis aguda, encefalomielitis aguda posinfecciosa y, a largo plazo, panencefalitis esclerosante subaguda. Las poblaciones más vulnerables son los menores de 5 años, los adultos jóvenes sin inmunización previa, las embarazadas y los inmunocomprometidos. La vacuna triple vírica (sarampión, rubeola y parotiditis) tiene una eficacia del 97% tras dos dosis y requiere una cobertura poblacional superior al 93% para alcanzar la inmunidad de rebaño. En México, la cobertura vacunal ha disminuido significativamente, lo que derivó en más de 12,000 casos confirmados y más de 33 defunciones durante el brote de 2025-2026, afectando mayoritariamente a niños no vacunados. La profilaxis posexposición con la vacuna triple vírica en un plazo de 72 horas, o con inmunoglobulina en un plazo de 6 días, está indicada para personas susceptibles de alto riesgo. La coordinación mundial, las campañas de vacunación sostenidas y una mayor vigilancia clínica siguen siendo fundamentales para frenar la transmisión.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the ongoing public health problem of measles, emphasizing its high contagiousness, prevention through vaccination, and the need for continuous surveillance. The research highlights the clinical presentation of measles, including the characteristic prodrome and rash, and outlines diagnostic methods such as serology, PCR, and viral culture. It also discusses the importance of supportive treatment, particularly the role of vitamin A in reducing mortality among pediatric patients. The study notes that complications occur in about 30% of cases, with common issues like diarrhea and otitis media and severe outcomes such as pneumonia and subacute sclerosing panencephalitis. Vulnerable populations include children under five, unvaccinated adults, pregnant women, and immunocompromised individuals. The paper underscores the critical role of vaccination coverage, with the triple viral vaccine showing 97% efficacy after two doses and requiring over 93% population coverage for herd immunity. It also references the significant decline in vaccination coverage in Mexico, leading to over 12,000 confirmed cases and more than 33 deaths during the 2025-2026 outbreak, primarily affecting unvaccinated children. The study concludes that global coordination, sustained vaccination campaigns, and enhanced clinical vigilance remain essential to control transmission.

papers.title_zh: Sarampión: de la eliminación al rebrote.文学修订与实际建议
papers.source_body_en: El sarampión es una enfermedad viral altamente contagiosa, prevenible por vacunación y de notificación obligatoria, que representa un problema de salud pública vigente. Su agente causal es el virus del sarampión (familia Paramyxoviridae), de serotipo único, transmitido por vía aérea con un número reproductivo básico de 12 a 18. La presentación clínica clásica incluye un pródromo de fiebre, tos, coriza y conjuntivitis, seguido de las manchas de Koplik y un exantema maculopapular cefalocaudal. El diagnóstico se confirma mediante serología (IgM específica), reacción en cadena de la polimerasa o cultivo viral. El tratamiento es fundamentalmente de soporte; en pacientes pediátricos, la vitamina A reduce la mortalidad hasta un 62%, por lo que está recomendada por la OMS en este grupo de pacientes. Las complicaciones ocurren en aproximadamente el 30% de los casos; las más frecuentes son diarrea (8%) y otitis media (7-9%), y las complicaciones graves incluyen neumonía, diarrea, encefalitis aguda, encefalomielitis aguda posinfecciosa y, a largo plazo, panencefalitis esclerosante subaguda. Las poblaciones más vulnerables son los menores de 5 años, los adultos jóvenes sin inmunización previa, las embarazadas y los inmunocomprometidos. La vacuna triple vírica (sarampión, rubeola y parotiditis) tiene una eficacia del 97% tras dos dosis y requiere una cobertura poblacional superior al 93% para alcanzar la inmunidad de rebaño. En México, la cobertura vacunal ha disminuido significativamente, lo que derivó en más de 12,000 casos confirmados y más de 33 defunciones durante el brote de 2025-2026, afectando mayoritariamente a niños no vacunados. La profilaxis posexposición con la vacuna triple vírica en un plazo de 72 horas, o con inmunoglobulina en un plazo de 6 días, está indicada para personas susceptibles de alto riesgo. La coordinación mundial, las campañas de vacunación sostenidas y una mayor vigilancia clínica siguen siendo fundamentales para frenar la transmisión.

papers.title: Comparative Performance of CNN and HOG-LBP-Based SVM for Mpox Classification
papers.abstract: Skin lesions caused by mpox may visually resemble those resulting from other skin diseases, making image-based classification a potential approach to support preliminary screening. This study aimed to compare the performance of a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and a Support Vector Machine (SVM) using combined Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG) and Local Binary Patterns (LBP) features for binary classification of mpox and other skin lesion images. The experimental dataset consisted of 224 unique original images, comprising 116 mpox images and 108 images of other conditions, including chickenpox and measles. The SVM employed a 23,250-dimensional HOG-LBP feature vector with a Radial Basis Function (RBF) kernel, whereas the CNN automatically learned visual representations from preprocessed RGB images. Both models were evaluated using identical stratified five-fold cross-validation partitions, with data splitting performed before augmentation and hyperparameter tuning conducted within the training partitions. Performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and specificity. The CNN achieved an average accuracy of 84.37%, precision of 88.73%, recall of 80.25%, F1-score of 84.06%, and specificity of 88.92%. Meanwhile, the SVM achieved 83.03%, 84.87%, 81.92%, 83.32%, and 84.28%, respectively. The results indicate that the CNN achieved higher performance in four evaluation metrics, while the SVM obtained slightly higher recall. These findings demonstrate that both approaches offer different classification strengths within the evaluated dataset. Nevertheless, further evaluation using independent datasets and more diverse skin lesion images is necessary to assess their generalizability before potential application in preliminary mpox screening.

The CNN achieved an average accuracy of 84.37%, precision of 88.73%, recall of 80.25%, F1-score of 84.06%, and specificity of 88.92%. Meanwhile, the SVM achieved 83.03%, 84.87%, 81.92%, 83.32%, and 84.28%, respectively. The results indicate that the CNN achieved higher performance in four evaluation metrics, while the SVM obtained slightly higher recall. These findings demonstrate that both approaches offer different classification strengths within the evaluated dataset. Nevertheless, further evaluation using independent datasets and more diverse skin lesion images is necessary to assess their generalizability before potential application in preliminary mpox screening.

papers.full_text: Hello Nature readers, would you like to get this Briefing in your inbox free every day? Sign up here. Voyager 1 is one light-day from Earth Today, as of 10:16 GMT, NASA’s Voyager 1 spacecraft has journeyed one light-day, or 25.9 billion kilometres, from Earth — farther than any human-made object has gone before. At this distance, signals from Earth’s surface travelling at light speed will take a full 24 hours to reach the craft. The trailblazing probe is expected to lose communications with Earth in 2029, when its plutonium power finally dies. But that time might not signal the end of Voyager 1’s contributions — the craft carries a golden record engraved with sights and sounds from Earth, an interspecies message for any aliens who might encounter it as it continues its journey. Alzheimer’s headset flops in critical trial A device that stimulates the brain with flickering light and rhythmic clicking sounds has failed to slow memory loss in people with Alzheimer’s disease. The Spectris AD headset is designed to induce brain activity called gamma waves, which have been linked to increased attention and memory. The results of a long-anticipated clinical trial showed that participants who used the device did not show robust improvements in their cognitive function after a year of treatment compared with those assigned to a sham treatment. The results were reported at the Clinical Trials on Alzheimer's Disease meeting on 16 November. US loses measles elimination status The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) has announced that the United States has lost its measles elimination status amid an outbreak that’s caused more than 5,700 infections and 10 deaths this year. The US had eliminated measles in 2000 after an intensive vaccination campaign. But declining vaccination rates in the past few years have left pockets of the population vulnerable to infection. “We’ve taken an enormous step back in public health,” says virologist Paul Offit. Measles has also been re-established in Mexico and Bolivia, PAHO announced. Features & opinion At-home microbiome tests Consumer tests that promise to reveal the full range of microbes living in your gut are taking off — but their results can vary widely. “This is an industry that’s running wild,” says genomicist Jacques Ravel, who co-authored a study that tested several providers. With regard to testing methods, he says, “there’s no standard”. But it’s hard to set those standards, writes journalist Amber Dance, who sent off her own stool to investigate the field. Part of the problem is that “there is no known ‘ground truth’ for a natural microbial sample”, she says. Quiz: can you spot a tortured phrase? Amid the tedium of investigating potentially fraudulent papers, “there is some light relief, thanks to some hilarious phrases used by authors seeking to avoid detection by plagiarism checkers”, writes research-integrity sleuth Dorothy Bishop. Bishop and Nature’s careers team have compiled a quiz to test your ability to match ‘tortured phrases’ — those that replace common words with synonyms in an attempt to skirt past plagiarism-detection software — with their original text. Take the Tortured Phrases Quiz The lost history of ‘Aquaterra’ From the Bering Strait to Doggerland, much of human history occurred in places that are now underwater, covered by the sea-level rise that occurs after ice ages. Geographer Jerome Dobson has dubbed this drowned land ‘Aquaterra’. It’s the site of many discoveries — such as Blinkerwall in the Baltic Sea, one of Europe’s oldest and largest Stone Age structures — and possibly many more to come. It also offers an interesting thought experiment: if we continue to drive global warming, what might future archaeologists make of our inundated world? The Atlantic | 29 min read, intermittent paywall Reference: Geographical Review paper (from 2014)

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the loss of measles elimination status in the United States, highlighting the decline in vaccination rates and the resulting public health concerns.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involves an analysis of public health data and a clinical trial of a device designed to stimulate brain activity in people with Alzheimer’s disease.
analysis.methods: The methods include a clinical trial of the Spectris AD headset, which uses flickering light and rhythmic clicking sounds to induce gamma waves, and an assessment of the device’s impact on cognitive function.
analysis.main_results: The clinical trial showed no robust improvements in cognitive function among participants using the Spectris AD headset compared to those using a sham treatment.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study concludes that the device failed to show significant cognitive benefits, suggesting that further research is needed to explore other methods for treating Alzheimer’s disease.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings have implications for the treatment of Alzheimer’s disease and highlight the need for continued research into effective interventions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the lack of a control group and the short duration of the trial, which may affect the generalizability of the results.

analysis.summary_en: The study analyzed the loss of measles elimination status in the US due to declining vaccination rates and evaluated a device for treating Alzheimer’s disease, finding no significant cognitive benefits.

papers.title: Perception of Socio-Cultural and Socio-Demographic Determinants ofVaccine-Preventable Disease Occurrence Among Mothers of Under-Five Children in Ilorin West Local Government Area, Kwara State
papers.abstract: Background: This study examined mothers' perceived and self-reported prevalence of vaccine-preventable diseases (VPDs), and their perceived socio-cultural and socio-demographic determinants of VPD occurrence, among children under five years in Ilorin West Local Government Area, Kwara State, Nigeria. Methodology: A quantitative descriptive survey design was adopted among mothers of children under five years resident in Ilorin West Local Government Area. A multistage sampling procedure involving stratification, simple random sampling, and systematic random sampling was used to select 418 respondents. A researcher structured questionnaire was used for data collection. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics and chi-square tests at 0.05 alpha level. Results: Mothers reported that vaccine-preventable diseases, principally measles (21.3%) and pertussis (16.3%), were perceived as prevalent among their children, with a pooled affirmative response rate of 9.1% across seven disease items. Mothers also held moderately positive socio-cultural beliefs, attitudes and practices favouring immunisation (grand mean = 2.68/4.00), and perceived sociodemographic factors, particularly maternal education, household income, and antenatal care attendance (grand mean = 2.76/4.00), as linked to VPD occurrence. Conclusion: Socio-cultural and socio-demographic factors remain influential, perceived determinants of the vaccine-preventable disease burden in Ilorin West Local Government Area, Kwara State.
